title: U.S. House · California's 29th District
area: The north-central San Fernando Valley in Los Angeles, including San Fernando, Van Nuys, Pacoima, Arleta, Panorama City, Sylmar, and parts of Sun Valley and North Hollywood. District lines were redrawn for the 2026 election under California Proposition 50.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 election cycle after voters approved Proposition 50 on November 4, 2025, a mid-decade redistricting measure.

Under California's top-two primary system, the two highest vote-getters in the June 2, 2026 primary advance regardless of party. Incumbent Democrat Luz Maria Rivas and fellow Democrat Angélica María Dueñas both advanced, so no Republican appears on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot for this seat.

candidates.name: Luz Maria Rivas
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative, CA-29 (since 2025); previously California State Assembly, 2018-2024
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary

priorities.text: Has conducted repeated oversight visits at immigration detention facilities in California and Texas and calls for the Dilley Immigration Processing Center to be shut down.
Says she is working to protect environmental justice communities in the San Fernando Valley from pollution linked to oil and gas operations.

positions.summary: Conducted a congressional oversight visit at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center and called for the Dilley Detention Facility to be shut down and for children not to be detained.
positions.quote: The Trump Administration must be held accountable for the trauma it is inflicting on immigrant families. Children should not be detained, and I am continuing to call for the Dilley Detention Facility to be shut down, immediately.

positions.summary: Cosponsored H.R. 3115, the Assault Weapons Ban of 2025, and H.R. 18, the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2025 (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 3069, the Medicare for All Act (119th Congress).
Cosponsored H.R. 2743, the Raise the Wage Act of 2025 (119th Congress).

Cosponsored H.R. 4099, the Ensuring Women’s Right to Reproductive Freedom Act, which prohibits interference under color of State law with the provision of interstate abortion services (119th Congress).

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee; Water, Wildlife and Fisheries Subcommittee) and the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology (Investigations and Oversight Subcommittee; Research and Technology Subcommittee) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).
Introduced the Methane Pollution Accountability Act, which would hold oil and gas companies accountable for pollutants released through venting, flaring, and leaking.
Introduced the Healing and Equity for Enforcement-Affected Residents and Trauma (HEART) Act of 2026 to fund mental-health services for communities affected by ICE immigration enforcement actions.

candidates.name: Angélica María Dueñas
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary as a fellow Democrat challenging the incumbent

priorities.text: Campaign website describes a "people first approach to governance" and lists peace, healthcare, jobs, housing, education, clean energy, immigration reform, criminal justice reform, and veteran care as her priorities.

positions.summary: Campaign website says she will never vote to send U.S. weapons or military aid to Israel.
positions.quote: I will never vote to send U.S. weapons or military aid to Israel.

positions.summary: Campaign website says she will vote for Medicare for All.
positions.quote: I will stand up and vote for Medicare for All, urgent climate action, and housing security for all

positions.summary: Campaign website lists ensuring access to abortion and reproductive healthcare among her issues.
positions.quote: Ensure access to abortion and reproductive healthcare, defend bodily autonomy, and protect every person’s freedom to make their own medical decisions without government interference.

positions.summary: Campaign website lists raising the minimum wage to a living wage among her workers' rights goals.
positions.quote: raise the minimum wage to a living wage

positions.summary: Campaign website calls for abolishing ICE.
positions.quote: the agency must be abolished and those responsible prosecuted

statements.quote: Billionaires borrow against stock to avoid income taxes. Any loan backed by stock should be treated and taxed as income, just like wages.
Clean energy now to lower costs, create local jobs, and protect the health of our communities and future generations.
Championing criminal justice reform: demilitarize police, boost accountability, end school-to-prison pipeline, ban private prisons, eliminate mandatory minimums, and reform use-of-force laws.
We advocate for stronger public schools, better teacher support, improved classrooms, protection from privatization, and universal pre-K and Head Start programs

researchNotes: Luz Maria Rivas has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; her official House issues subpages (economy, energy, health, education, veterans) are placeholders with no text, so positions and priorities here are drawn from her press releases instead. Her federal floor votes and FEC totals are added separately by script. Angélica María Dueñas has also not completed the 2026 survey; her platform quotes come from Ballotpedia's page, which excerpts her campaign website from her 2024 run. As of this check, her current live campaign website (same domain) no longer displays that platform text, so the quotes are cited to Ballotpedia (s3) rather than the live site. Angélica María Dueñas: the live campaign site (angelica4congress.com) now carries issue text, which is the basis for the positions and statements added; no Ballotpedia survey. Biography expansion: Rivas's biography draws on her official House pages and Ballotpedia; Angélica María Dueñas has no official or news biography beyond Ballotpedia's profile, so her biography is limited to what it states.
